falsifier: the widened bound recovers no must-find, or its new matches are mostly false by meaning, or mean element_jaccard over matches falls by more than the matches it gains
hypothesis: widening #441's bound from one hop to two recovers must-finds the bound cuts, at a small cost in element precision and without false matches
intervention: re-ran fan_in over the archived lane proposals of the four STRIDE Baselines (52 case-runs) with ModelIndex.reach as shipped (V0), applied twice (V1) and unbounded (V2), carried each kept draft's archived critic verdict by title, and re-scored. V0 reproduced the archived drafts in 45 of 52; the 7 differences are older flow-ID spellings in archived reports, not the bound. V1 against V0: must-finds matched 201 to 206 (+5, all correct by meaning), matches 381 to 394 (12 correct by meaning, 2 false: case 01 ref 9 and case 13 ref 3), one doubtful match lost (case 05 ref 13), unlisted 86 to 82, mean element_jaccard over matches 0.420 to 0.413, mean elements per claim 2.71 to 2.81. V2 adds one more must-find (case 02 ref 5) over V1. 7 of the 12 correct gains are repudiation claims whose record store sits two hops from the flow the grounds cite
reconsider_when: the maintainer decides whether to widen the bound; #441's rule or the identity rule's element half changes
scope: four archived Baselines on their own configurations, today's fan-in code, critic verdicts carried by title (a critic shown the wider draft could rule differently), unseen new drafts 2 of about 470; deterministic, so no run-to-run spread applies to the replay itself
signature: fan-in narrows a kept draft's elements off the reference's place, because they are more than one hop from the claim's grounds

falsifier: the replayed critic changes the verdict on any draft
hypothesis: a critic sent the identical archived request rules every draft as it did in the run, so a carried ruling (E7, descendants) stands for what the critic would say
intervention: run.py critic-replay on case 07's 2026-09-24 analysis run (b8a325d), one call, with the rebuilt request tested byte for byte against the graph's: 10 of 11 verdicts agree; D-01 moved from needs-info to rejected
reconsider_when: repeats of the critic replay give its spread; the critic prompt changes
scope: one call, one case, 11 drafts, terra via openrouter openai/flex; one disagreement in eleven on an identical request is run-to-run variance in the critic, not a rate
signature: the critic's verdicts on one case's drafts, replayed from the archive

falsifier: the replayed critic rejects the same ten drafts again, so the rejections are a stable judgement a critic prompt change can be measured against
hypothesis: the ten critic rejections #1075 records on Baseline 6bff717 are a stable judgement, so a critic.md change can be priced by replaying those drafts
intervention: run.py critic-replay on cases 04, 05, 06, 07, 10 and 11 of Baseline 6bff717, one call each, with the job-wide keys rendered from the report's model (#1197). The critic's own text is unchanged since 6bff717. Seven of the ten rejections moved (six to needs-info, 07 E-01 to confirmed); 05 T-03, 06 I-01 and 07 T-01 stayed rejected. 58 of 85 verdicts agree, and 8 archived needs-info verdicts moved to rejected. Scored today: references 48 -> 50, must-finds 28 -> 25.
reconsider_when: the critic rules a draft more than once, or its verdict becomes a function of the model rather than one sample
scope: six calls, one per case, 85 drafts, terra via openrouter openai/flex; one sample per case, so each verdict move is one draw, not a rate
signature: the critic's rejections of matched drafts, replayed from the Baseline archive

falsifier: the expected majority-of-3 agreement, estimated from five verdicts per draft, is below 0.90
hypothesis: a critic that rules each draft three times and keeps the majority (a three-way split keeps needs-info) agrees with itself on at least 0.90 of the 85 E9 drafts, the adoption rule #1199 declared before the run
intervention: run.py critic-replay three more times on cases 04, 05, 06, 07, 10 and 11 of Baseline 6bff717 (18 calls), so each of 85 drafts has five verdicts: the archived one, E9 and three new. Single-call agreement over all sample pairs is 0.846 (E9's 58 of 85 was a low draw). Expected majority-of-3 agreement: plug-in 0.903, jackknife bias-corrected 0.891, Dirichlet(1/2) posterior 0.812. 26 of 85 drafts took more than one verdict; 117 of 131 disagreeing pairs are needs-info against rejected, 9 confirmed against needs-info, 5 confirmed against rejected.
reconsider_when: the critic's needs-info against rejected choice becomes a rule in code, or the critic model or its sampling changes
scope: six cases, 85 STRIDE drafts, five verdicts each, terra via openrouter openai/flex; the plug-in estimate is biased high with five samples, so the bias-corrected 0.891 decides. The margin is small: about one draft in a hundred
signature: the critic gives a different verdict for the same draft when the same request is sent again

falsifier: the archived reasons of the 26 unstable E10 drafts name no missing premise, or the stable needs-info verdicts carry subject entries as often as the unstable ones
hypothesis: the drafts whose verdict moves between needs-info and rejected are the drafts whose argument depends on a fact that has no attribute in the model, so critic.md's two answers for that case (needs-info with a subject entry, or rejected for reasoning) are what the critic alternates between
intervention: offline read of the 26 E10 drafts with more than one verdict against Baseline 6bff717: draft grounds, archived verdict and reason, related_unknowns. Every one of the 11 archived rejections says the draft depends on a fact the model does not state: integrity inferred from an unknown encryption_at_rest (3), authorization inferred from an unknown authentication (2), an audit record (3, two inferred from a graph-shape absence), request capacity (1), merge or release authority (2). Archived needs-info verdicts carry a subject entry in 8 of 14 unstable drafts against 2 of 46 stable ones. All 46 stable needs-info drafts cite an unknown-attribute ground and all 11 stable confirmed drafts cite none. 18 of the 26 unstable drafts match a reference claim in the Baseline's scoring, 7 of them must-finds; a rule that ruled the class needs-info every time gains about 2.4 must-finds and 7.8 matches in expectation over the six cases
reconsider_when: critic.md changes how it rules a draft that depends on a fact with no attribute in the model
scope: 85 STRIDE drafts, six cases, one Baseline; the replays kept only their verdicts, so reasons are the archived call's alone; the gain is an expectation from five samples a draft, under the Baseline's scorer
signature: the critic gives a different verdict for the same draft when the same request is sent again

falsifier: one-call agreement across all pairs of the three new replays is below 0.90
hypothesis: with the verdict decided in code from the critic's fields (PR #1204), three critic replays of the same six cases agree pairwise on at least 0.90 of drafts, the rule #1202 declared before the run
intervention: run.py critic-replay three times on cases 04, 05, 06, 07, 10 and 11 of Baseline 6bff717 at b2e2d62 (18 calls), against the three E10 rounds under the old prompt. Pairwise agreement 0.969 (old 0.839 over the same 255 pairs); drafts with more than one verdict 4 (old 20). Verdicts over 255: confirmed 29, needs-info 225, rejected 1 (old 35, 180, 40). All 13 archived rejections in these cases were for reasoning. Expected kept drafts that match a reference claim: 52.7 of 53 (old 42.7), must-finds 32 of 32 (old 28.7); unmatched drafts kept 32 of 32 (old 29). 12 drafts changed majority, 11 of them rejected to needs-info, including the three stable #1075 kills 05 T-03, 06 I-01 and 07 T-01
reconsider_when: a sweep shows drafts the reasoning check should have stopped, or critic.md changes step 1
scope: six cases, 85 STRIDE drafts, three samples each under each rule, terra via openrouter openai/flex, scored against the Baseline's matches; the reasoning check now fires on 1 of 255 verdicts, so its value as a filter is unmeasured here
signature: the critic gives a different verdict for the same draft when the same request is sent again

falsifier: rejections remove matched drafts more often than drafts voted not real, severity changes move away from the reference level more often than toward it, or confidence does not order the match rate
hypothesis: each job the critic does beside the verdict improves the report against the reference set: its rejections remove unmatched drafts, its severity changes move toward the reference level, and its confidence rating predicts which claims match
intervention: re-scored the four Baselines (2198870, 6bff717, d3f1898, d4edd64; 52 case-runs, 867 kept claims) with today's scorer and read each critic job against the matches and the vote standings. Rejections: 30 kills; 17 removed a draft that matches a reference claim (8 must-finds), none removed a draft a person voted not real, 1 lane kill was a real lane error. Severity: on 438 matched claims the critic changed 45 levels, 34 further from the reference level and 11 closer, in every Baseline; exact agreement fell from 199 (draft) to 184 (ruled). Most changes lowered the level. Confidence: share of kept claims that are real (matched or voted pooled) is 0.65 high, 0.59 medium, 0.52 low; 714 of 867 claims are low. Verdict: 0.62 of confirmed and 0.53 of needs-info claims are real. Recommendation soundness has no reference to grade against
reconsider_when: a person reviews the reference severity levels, or the critic's severity or confidence instruction changes
scope: four Baselines under the old critic prompt; only 12 kept claims carry a not-real vote, so realness rests mostly on reference matches; the reference severity levels are agent-authored and no person reviewed them
signature: the critic changes a claim's severity, confidence or fate, and nothing measured says the change helps

falsifier: fewer matched drafts are kept, or the archived critic rejected a draft the maintainer voted not real that the new critic keeps
hypothesis: across all 13 cases, the critic at bcd69e1 (code-decided verdict, no severity step) keeps at least as many drafts that match a reference claim as the archived critic, and loses no stop on a claim a person voted not real

Against the archived verdicts: must-find drafts kept 61 -> 64 of 65, expected 48 -> 55 of 55, unmatched unvoted 0 -> 4 of 6. Rejections 17 -> 3 (01 T-04 and 08 T-01 unmatched, 02 D-01 a must-find). All 12 drafts the maintainer voted not real were kept by the archived critic and are kept now. 13 drafts moved confirmed -> needs-info (6 must-finds); confirmed fell from 36 to 24 of 185. The replay prints statuses only, so why they moved is not visible
reconsider_when: a sweep runs the full graph at or after bcd69e1, or the critic prompt changes
